description.purpose: Scope marker of the session keeper: bundles the channel-generation state and the two passes that move it — the stamp in the ingress path and the nightly close. THE HIVE IS THE ADDRESS: a caller sends to the keeper and names a lane, never a cell inside it. A session is a phone call on a channel: it begins with a turn, it ends deterministically, and everything downstream only reads the id.
description.use_when: One per agent surface, in front of the context assembly. Wire the parent's edges TO THE HIVE PATH — see meclaw-overview § Die Hive-Grenze. `params.ports` is empty and therefore sealed: a mutation reaching inside is rejected with hive_port_boundary. The keeper is an island until an edge crosses into it.
description.not_in_scope: No conversation content and no context assembly -- the turns live in the collector's window. No judgement about whether a conversation is over: the close is a timer plus an idle threshold, never a model call. Nothing is deleted; a closed generation stays as a row.
description.contract_in: in_turn — an inbound turn from the surface; the caller MUST promote the channel identity to context.channel, or every chat lands on the channel 'default'. in_sweep — an operator-forced sweep outside the night. Any other route is refused by the hive rather than delivered to a cell that would not know it.
description.contract_out: turn — a stamped turn, carrying hop.session_id, for the context assembly (promote the id to context on that edge; that IS the stamp). close — a finished session, carrying hop.session_id and hop.channel, for whoever consumes one (the collector's in_close lane).
